decisions.evidence: Skeptic's premise is wrong: this is not an STL copy loop. It walks a vector of 0x38-byte elements, unpacks two SSO strings per element (+0x20 key, -0x1c value, both with the 0xf capacity check) and calls FUN_578410(ctx,key,value) per element - i.e. application code applying each parsed property. Sole caller is FUN_57af10, the 'Requirements'/'applytoall' parser; sole callee FUN_578410 is inside slice 12's run 0x5782b0-0x57af10 which slice 12 labelled lib:other and flagged as continuing into slice 13. So it stays with the parser object, not the STL block that starts right after it at 0x57b520. Keep lib:other for run consistency with slice 12; 'shell' is the second choice, lib:crt is wrong.

std::basic_string ctor from char*: sets capacity(+0x18)=0xf, length(+0x14)=0, terminates SSO buffer at +4, strlen-inlines the argument, then calls FUN_57bc90 (string assign(ptr,len)). Canonical MSVC 7.1 16-byte-SSO layout; 3 callers, all container plumbing. lib:crt, matching assign_20's lib:crt for the string throw helpers 0x638e74/0x638eb4 that this run calls.

std::basic_string::_Tidy: 'if (capacity(+0x18) > 0xf) free(ptr(+4))' then capacity=0xf, length=0, buffer[0]=0. Pure SSO teardown, 21 callers across the whole C++ region (incl. the EH funclets at 0x6392ea that assign_20 already noted target this object). Compiler-shipped STL, lib:crt.

std::map<string,T>::operator[]: FUN_57c530 (lower_bound) -> if result != _Myhead(+4), SSO-unpack the node key at +0x10/+0x24 and compare with FUN_57ce10; on no-match clear a temp string (FUN_57b830 with 0,0xffffffff) and insert via FUN_57ba50, then return node+0x28 (the mapped value). Textbook _Tree machinery, not parser logic.
std::map<string,T>::find: same lower_bound (FUN_57c530) + node-key SSO unpack (+0x10/+0x24) + FUN_57ce10 compare, returning the node or _Myhead(+4). Identical _Tree pattern to 0x57b6e0; lib:crt.

std::basic_string::assign(const basic_string&,off,count): range-checks off against source length(+0x14) calling FUN_638e74 (_Xran, 'invalid string position') and the npos overflow path calling FUN_638eb4 (_Xlen, 'string too long') - both already labelled lib:crt in assign_20 - then grows via FUN_57c6d0 and does the rep-movsd copy with the 0x10 SSO branch. Unambiguous STL string member, 9 callers.

std::vector<T>::insert(iterator,value): computes the insertion index as (pos - _Myfirst)/0x38, calls FUN_57be20 (the insert/grow routine) with count 1, then rebuilds and returns the iterator as _Myfirst + index*0x38. Pure container arithmetic over a 0x38-byte element; lib:crt.

std::vector<T>::clear/~vector: loops [_Myfirst(+4), _Mylast(+8)) in 0x38-byte strides calling the element destructor FUN_5785b0, frees the block and nulls +4/+8/+0xc. Generic container teardown; lib:crt.

References the literal MSVC STL diagnostic 'invalid vector<T> subscript' and throws it via FUN_5782b0 + __CxxThrowException@8 (out_of_range ctor path with FUN_57bc90 building the message string). Compiler-shipped _Xran for vector::at; lib:crt per the CRT-fencing rule.

std::basic_string::assign(const char*,size_t): operates on +4 buffer / +0x14 length / +0x18 capacity with the <0x10 SSO branch, grows through FUN_57c6d0 and delegates the copy to FUN_57b830, with _Xlen (FUN_638eb4, lib:crt) on overflow. 13 callers spread across the whole C++ region - shared STL plumbing, not parser glue.

713-byte std::vector<T>::_Insert_n/grow for a 0x38-byte element: operator_new for the new block, uninitialized copy/move with element ctor+dtor (FUN_57be00/FUN_5785b0), rollback through the Catch funclets at 0x57bfec/0x57c0a8, and the length overflow call into FUN_57c130 ('vector<T> too long'). No Blam strings or data refs; lib:crt.
References the literal MSVC STL diagnostic 'vector<T> too long' and throws it (_Xlen for vector) via FUN_5782b0/FUN_57bc90/__CxxThrowException@8. Compiler-shipped STL; lib:crt.

References the literal MSVC STL diagnostic 'map/set<T> too long' (_Tree::_Xlen) and is the _Tree insert path (node alloc FUN_57cc30, rebalance helpers FUN_57cb10/FUN_57cb90) that throws it. Compiler-shipped STL; lib:crt.

744-byte _Tree::erase: references the literal MSVC STL diagnostic 'invalid map/set<T> iterator', uses the same node helpers (FUN_57cb10 _Min/_Max, FUN_57cb70, FUN_57cb90) and frees nodes. Unambiguous STL red-black-tree internals; lib:crt.

_Destroy backward range loop: walks elements in 0x38-byte strides and calls the string clear helper FUN_57b830(p,0,0xffffffff) twice per element (offsets +0 and +0x1c), i.e. the two std::strings inside each map/vector value_type. Compiler-generated destroy-range for the container; same STL run, lib:crt.

EH funclet (Ghidra Catch@) belonging to FUN_57cf50: unwinds the partially-constructed 0x38-byte element range calling FUN_5785b0 per element then rethrows via __CxxThrowException@8. Compiler-generated unwind code for the STL container run; lib:crt. It is also the last function of the STL block - the genuinely Blam/Gearbox config code resumes at 0x57cfe0 (CpuSpeed bounds check) / 0x57d080 / 0x57d410 ('config.txt', 'ForceShader', 'Unknown property in config.txt'), so the run boundary should move from 0x57d340 down to 0x57cfa3 as the skeptic says.
